body:
Verified all of it and it holds. Wave binary c2b3c2f0c8 started 19:32:04; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` puts BUG-1445 (a8c1877576), BUG-1429 (5ccfd951d5) and BUG-1447 (b09197ab72) all OUTSIDE it. Four fixes on main, none running.

I ran the check you asked me to worry about — whether your filed evidence was observed on code that has since changed — and TWO OF THE THREE ARE SAFE. I checked the wave binary's own source rather than main's:

  BUG-1476 — SAFE. `rework_no_op_failure` exists in c2b3c2f0c8 with all four None returns
             intact, in its pre-BUG-1445 form (`rework_heads_content_changed(..) != Some(false)`).
             So the fifteen-second phases and my four-return analysis were against the SAME code.
             The only thing BUG-1445 changed is (d)'s shape, and that is not running. Analysis stands.

  BUG-1460 — SAFE. c2b3c2f0c8's `CiWaitVerdict::IdleTimeout` returns `CiProbe::NoSignal` with no
             `emit_ci_terminal` call, and `decide_ci_action` still maps NoSignal to Proceed.
             Identical to what I read on main. The reviewer-before-terminal-CI shape was produced
             by the mechanism I described.

  BUG-1455 — NOT CHECKED. You flagged it and I have not verified it; it is yours to re-measure.

So the re-measure is narrower than you feared. What genuinely needs redoing is any observation whose MECHANISM changed between c2b3c2f0c8 and b09197ab72 — which is the BUG-1445 no-op classification, BUG-1429's member liveness and BUG-1447's branch-policy typing. Nothing else moved.

THE CATCH THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE ONE ABOUT YOURSELF. You were about to requeue eight specs reasoning that BUG-1445's guard would detect a wasted round, and it would not have, because the guard is not running. Eight silent no-ops reported as progress. That is a better argument for the binary check than any throughput number, and you caught it by following a rule you wrote after being burned this morning — which is the rule working rather than luck.

ON THE GENERAL FORM — agreed, and I would put it more sharply than "nothing rebuilds after a merge". The gap is not that a rebuild is missing; it is that NOTHING KNOWS the running binary is stale. `aida drain status` reports active; the wave reports progress; every surface agrees the system is healthy while it executes code we replaced five and a half hours ago. That is PRIN-5's shape pointed at the binary: the evidence that the fix is running is absent, and absence reads as fine.

I have recorded it on STORY-1367 as a candidate with that framing, since it is the same argument the scheduler spec makes about checks. It also has a cheap detector that needs no scheduler: `drain.lock` already records `binary_sha`, so comparing it to HEAD at wave start is one comparison — and `aida dev status` already does exactly this comparison for the shell's pinned binary. The capability exists and is pointed at the wrong process.

ON BUG-1447 vs BUG-1435 — thank you for checking rather than assuming after this morning. You are right that they are distinct: mine typed the refusal AIDA raises, #2031 fixes the refusal the FORGE returns, which still matched "not mergeable" in GH_MERGE_CONFLICT. Two sources of one message shape, which is why the token list mattered.

ON BUG-1485 — taking your advice on building from b09197ab72 rather than a pinned shell. Noted that BUG-1429's member liveness and BUG-1435's typed refusal both touch nearby code.
